memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Any bed the man with a discharge lies on will be unclean, and anything he sits on will be unclean. Anyone who touches his bed must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.'" - Lev 15:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
His bed. His chair. And now anyone who touches them.

Imagine living this. Every seat you sit on becomes off-limits. Every bed you rest in must be avoided. Your presence in the house rearranges where everyone else can sit. You are not only ill — you are a complication for everyone you love.

That is one of the heaviest burdens of long-term illness, and people rarely say it out loud: the sense of being a problem. Not just suffering, but causing inconvenience. Needing lifts, needing help, needing patience. Many chronically ill believers carry more guilt about being a burden than they do about anything else.

If that is you, hear this clearly. God gave these laws to protect ceremonial access to the tabernacle. He never said the sick person was a nuisance. And when Jesus met the sick, He never once treated them as an interruption.

Paul writes that the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable, and that God has given greater honour to the parts that lacked it (1 Cor 12:22-24). Indispensable. That is God's word about the person everyone else finds inconvenient.

You are not a complication in God's household. You are a member of it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you feel like a burden to the people around you?
2. How does God's view of the "weaker" members challenge how you see yourself?
3. Who in your life needs to hear they are not an inconvenience?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You never treat the suffering as an interruption. Where I feel like a burden, remind me that I am indispensable to Your body, and give me grace to receive help. Amen.
